# Taking on a Black Ark

*Pages PDF 34-56*

## **A Year at Sea**
## **Taking on a Black Ark**
Dark elves divide the year into 100 day seasons dedicated to the gods, the seasons of Blood (Khaine), Despair (Ereth Khial), Decadence (Atharti), and Savagery (Anath Raema). Even a dysfunctional society has festivals to respect the gods and mark the passing of the year. 

## **Season of Blood**

- **Death Night** — the followers of Khaine venture out to slaughter (see page 112) on the night known as Geheimnisnacht on the Imperial Calendar. 

- **Draich na Anlar** — ‘Reaping of Souls’, a week-long festival sacred to Khaine. Witch elves compete in bloody ritual combat across the ark. Highborn Druchii sacrifice their precious captives to placate the god and spare their household on Death Night, which falls at the end of the week. 

- **Equinox of Rain** — festival at the autumn equinox to celebrate the ascension of Aenarion to the Phoenix Throne. Captives and other offerings are burned on bonfires atop the ark’s tallest towers. 

## **Season of Despair**

- **Hanil Khar** — ‘The Bearing of Chains’. At the start of winter, all on the ark must swear loyalty to the fleetmaster. 

- **Tuanhain** — ‘Time of Spirits’, sacred to Ereth Khial. Spirits are permitted to leave mirai for a single night to haunt their family and acquaintances. On this night, elven ghosts may be seen flocking around the towers. 

## **Season of Decadence**

- **Feast of Reprieve** — a celebration at the beginning of spring, when the Vanguard Spires and Fleetmaster’s Bastion ring with cruel laughter and revelry. Helbane holds a masked ball, where the most exalted in ark society don daemonic or absurd masks. 

- **Time of Abandon** — three days leading to the spring equinox, a time of debauchery dedicated to Atharti. Other than the most devout Khainites, the whole ark indulges in pleasurable excess. 

## **Season of Savagery**

- **Day of Claws** — holy day for Anath Raema at the height of the season. Beastmasters lead the ark’s highborn to hunt captives released onto an island, or the ark itself if too far from land. 

In addition to these events, the Storm Witch Neryssa hosts ceremonies for Mathlann whenever Mannslieb (called _Sariour_ in Druhir) is full, during which she casts sacrifices into the ocean. 

The _Temple of Spite_ is designed to inspire many types of scenario for your games, including longer campaigns in which the Characters deal with its denizens and spend time on the ark itself. The following outlines illustrate two potential types of campaign. **The Seaborne Citadel** focuses on _Temple of Spite_ primarily as a setting, where the Characters must survive in a hostile city far out to sea. **On Black Tides** showcases the ark’s warbands as they plan an invasion of the Empire. As GM you’ll need to add detail from the rest of the book to flesh out the campaign and adapt for your party. 

## **The Seaborne Citadel**
The _Temple of Spite_ is a setting rather than a ship. Whole campaigns could play out without ever leaving the vessel, and Helbane’s designs on Tor Elithis might sweep your party into adventure anywhere the ark travels. 

## **Part 1 — Horror on the Horizon**
Tales of attacks on the coastline reach Salzenmund, a Bretonnian village was wiped out, sudden raids harried coastal settlements in Ostland and Nordland, and a watchtower burned close to Hargendorf. When the wolfship _Fist of Mandred_ is lost north of Kriedeklippe Bight, Sea Lord Köhler grows concerned for his burgeoning fleet, and Salzenmund’s Nordland Naval Chamber hires the party to investigate. 

The party can uncover rumours and clues to the origins of the raids: 

- Sailors in the towns of Dietershafen, Hargendorf, and Neues Emskrank claim an uncharted island has appeared in the Sea of Claws. Some blame the influence of Chaos from the north, others talk of the legendary black arks. 

- Fishermen and coastal communities say bands of elves have been seen abroad at night. Fearful locals lynch an Eonir traveller in Wilhelmskoog. 

- At the Nordwrack Temple on Wrecker’s Point, two elves wrapped in scaled cloaks land to pay their respects to Mathlann. The strange visitors do not harm any worshippers, though their forbidding appearance and manner certainly leaves an impression. 

- A drunken Norscan trader drowns his sorrows after losing most of his crew and cargo. He tells everyone that a black ark has come and will bring ruin to the lands of men. 

Khaine’s Eyes scout the northern coast for a secure landing place for a major raid. The spy Myrentha Selkarth accompanies them, then travels west to Marienburg to meet with Harzeth Duskmantle. She leaves a trail which the Characters can follow or discover from Eonir waywatchers. 

In Marienburg, the party can follow clues to Duskmantle and expose him as a spy. He escapes on a stolen horse through the Wasteland to Harl Cove on Wrecker’s Point, a hidden dark elf landing, where Captain Flariel takes him back to the _Temple of Spite_ . The ark is visible on the horizon, emerging from the mist. After a fight, the corsairs may capture the Characters or they could escape with the knowledge of the black ark and its rough location. In this case, Marienburg’s elves plan to inform Ulthuan, offer the party a considerable reward to investigate on their behalf and, if possible, bring back the crew of _Isha’s Lament_ , an elven merchant ship taken by the dark elves. 

## **Part 2 — Life in Chains**
If they were not captured, the Characters have the option to walk away, attempt to board, or assault the black ark. If they approach, three doomreavers attack their vessel, so it is likely they are taken prisoner and must now find a way to break free from their cells. This is a prison scenario, where the Characters meet captive NPCs from across the world, making allies and adversaries amongst their fellow prisoners. They face fights with captured beastmen, and must negotiate with others who could be enemy or tenuous ally, such as Thraeg Icejaw (see page 17). 

During captivity, the Characters are put to work across the ark, doing punishing labour or, if they have specific skills, tasks suited to their character. A dwarf might be forced to work as an artisan, a warrior taken to fight in the arena, or an entertainer coerced to perform for the amusement of mocking nobles. This is an opportunity to learn the layout and social hierarchy of the ark as they are dragged around by their handlers. 

The party have several options to escape: 

- Organise rebellion amongst the captives, to overwhelm the guards or create a distraction as they break their bonds 

To explore the ark, they can secure disguises by waylaying individual dark elves or favoured captives. Several Norscans seem to be on board as guests of the fleetmaster, which presents an option for disguise. If they use their new knowledge of the ark’s society, they would be wise to find a dark elf patron who can protect them, in exchange for doing their bidding. 

## **Part 3 — Amongst the Druchii**
No longer in chains, the Party can properly explore the physical and social structure of _Temple of Spite_ . By listening, observing, and talking with servants and others, they can uncover Duriath Helbane’s ambitions and the ark’s vulnerabilities. They can discern the rival factions and conflicting agendas and use that knowledge to find temporary support: 

- **Helbane vs mutineers.** Traitors that survived the purge vow revenge against the fleetmaster. 

- **Hawks vs dissenters.** Not every Druchii believes an assault on Tor Elithis serves their interests. 

- **Khainites vs everyone.** While all dark elves pay respect to Khaine, the zealots in Valeth’s Palace are beloved by nobody on the ark. 

- **Slaaneshi cultists.** If the identity of the cultists became widely known, the Black Convocation would be sorely tested. 

- **Captain vs captain.** Reavers continually compete for prestige and wealth. 

- **Highborn vs highborn.** Dark elf nobles are particularly prone to intrigue and mutual betrayal. 

Frustrating their investigations is Guardmaster Vranek Umberkill, a dogged investigator who knows the party are loose, despite what his arrogant superiors in the warhost tell him. This can be played as an urban intrigue scenario, using the ark as a sandbox, where the Characters must exercise discretion and use subterfuge to avoid scrutiny. They may need to adopt fake personae (such as Norscans or captives), manipulate their patron to keep themselves safe, or perhaps prove their usefulness to gain rare privileges for non-Druchii inhabitants of the ark. They never know if they can trust anyone and must continually prove their value to those protecting them. 

- Slip away during their work 

- Demonstrate a valuable skill or knowledge that catches the eye of a potential dark elf patron, who will insist they enter their service 

- Bribe or manipulate an overseer or guard 

Once they escape, the party are probably going to be fugitives on board. They must find ways to survive and elude recapture. In the depths, they can find hidden caverns where they can set up a base from where they can steal food and fresh water. 

The party encounter a small delegation of Norscans on board, a band of savage Bjornlings hoping to negotiate an alliance with Duriath Helbane. They should also learn about the three nexuses and their importance in keeping the ark afloat. Eventually, the Characters hear from an intoxicated corsair that the ark is bound for the island of Rrinnhasha. Helbane intends to assault the high elf outpost there as a preparatory exercise for attacking Tor Elithis. 

## **The Island of Rrinnhasha**
The dark elves will never be content ruling only Naggaroth, for they consider all Ulthuan to be their birthright, but there are two regions of their sundered home that they desire above all. 

The Shadowlands are the remains of ancient Nagarythe, where Aenarion held court at Anlec, and from these lands the ancestors of the Nagarythe sprung. Though the dark elves have invaded Nagarythe many times, no conquest has endured. Each time Anlec has been rebuilt, high elf soldiers have cast it down. 

North of Anlec lies the Blighted Isle, site of the Shrine of Khaine, within which can be found the weapon Widowmaker. Many wars have been fought across its skull-strewn plains, and at night, the spirits of the dead battle anew, forever captured by the will of Khaine. The struggle for the Shrine of Khaine is symbolic of the struggle in the soul of all elves. None can say how it will end, or indeed, if it ever will. 

North of Ulthuan is an archipelago of scattered islands of varying size. Some are inhabited by high elves or dark elf encampments, while others remain barren. During the elven civil war, the high elves fought a decisive naval engagement against the Naggarothi amongst these islands. Asur scholars argue that the First Battle of Deloth’s Shoals, fought in −2741 IC, was pivotal in the defeat of Malerion’s followers. 

The islands have been disputed territory for centuries, and the dark elves target them to provide a foothold for raids on Ulthuan, seeking to secure their most prized target, the Blighted Isle. In turn, Asur forces repel the Druchii and re-establish settlements and outposts, before coming under attack once again. 

Rrinnhasha is an island that lies to the northwest of the Blighted Isle. For thousands of years, it was sparsely inhabited by sea elves, until the forces of Hag Queen Cynhaef invaded the island in 1128 IC and wiped out the population. The Druchii considered this a great victory for the Cult of Khaine, and the isle was abandoned for centuries until phoenix King Finubar ordered a new outpost raised on the ruins of Feiss Mabdon. The settlers restored the town in 2368 IC, clearing out nests of harpies and the lairs of monsters, building new walls, and raising a memorial shrine on Chulin Meadow where many hundreds of their kinfolk were slaughtered. This small community and garrison hopes to restore the island as a powerful outpost of Ulthuan and parties of high elves now venture to the northeast coast, where the former port of Giaf Gahdion lies in ruins. It’s desolation is a testament to the hag queen’s atrocities. 

The dark elves recently discovered Asur attempts to recolonise Rrinnhasha. The island has strategic and symbolic value to the Druchii, so the fleetmaster that retakes Feiss Mabdon could earn more than a flicker of favour from Malerion. 

## **Part 4 — Landfall**
Duriath Helbane and Hag Queen Kheitalla agree that destroying the outpost in Feiss Mabdon is a fitting display of power, a howled prayer to Khaine, and a test of _Temple of Spite’s_ martial strength. They plan an invasion and order the whole ark to prepare for battle. 

The Characters could be pressed into joining the military action. They might be dragged ashore as captives, to carry provisions and undertake labour for the invading force, or a dark elf patron might insist they land with them, to act as their eyes and ears. They could sneak ashore by stowing away in one of the wrackholds or ravenships ferrying troops to the shore. 

Many of Helbane’s warbands land on Rrinnhasha, with Khaine’s Eyes scouting the land, Valerion’s Blackswords seeking Elven patrols to kill, the Nightwake Company joining raids on the coast, and a host of Khainites determined to reprise Cynhaef ’s campaign of slaughter. If the party are clever, they can goad rival factions into open conflict, or draw them away from the ark and Helbane’s discipline. By further weakening _Temple of Spite’s_ precarious alliances, they can stoke political unrest or desertion. 

The Characters could race ahead of the despoilers to warn the Feiss Mabdon garrison. There they meet an elven scholar, Thalanis Dawnbloom, who holds the key to sinking _Temple of Spite_ . After escaping imprisonment on the ark _Endless Torment_ , he has studied black arks and the enchantments worked into their structure. Dawnbloom can teach them about the nexuses and how to disrupt this flow of _Dhar_ that buoys up the ark. 

Another useful contact in Feiss Mabdon is Ithamar Starblade, a Sea Guard commander. If the Characters reach him in time, he despatches a fast hawkship to summon a fleet to attack the black ark and protect Rrinnhasha. 

Whether the outpost falls depends on the Characters. They can take this opportunity to escape the _Temple of Spite_ , or seize a chance to destroy it. Whatever their decision or Rrinnhasha’s fate, Duriath Helbane decides he can no longer rely on his military alone and he needs to strike a real blow against Ulthuan. He persuades his Norscan guests that they should form a huge warhird to scour the kingdom of Cothique of every last soul. 

## **Part 5 — the Last Voyage**
Events of the last part of the campaign are contingent on what has happened so far and the actions taken by the Characters. 

- They may have stoked up tensions amongst the dark elves, with different factions in open conflict. This could lead to Helbane’s downfall, or provide a distraction for their actions on board. 

- Powerful individuals may be spoiling for a new mutiny, spurred on by the Characters’ intrigues. They might push this forward or further weaken the ark by exposing the conspiracy to Helbane. 

- If they met Ithamar Starblade, there may be a powerful high elf fleet gathering to attack the _Temple of Spite_ , and Helbane may order several of his corsair ships to intercept them. 

- The Characters may know captives ready to rise against their captors, with the right leadership from themselves or a chosen leader. 

- The Characters should have discovered the nature of the nexuses keeping the ark afloat and learned from Thalanis Dawnbloom or another source how they could untangle the magic. 

As the high elf fleet attacks and the inhabitants turn on one another, the party can destroy the nexuses and sink the ark. Alternately, a particularly devious party could employ more subtle means of destruction, such as persuading Helbane to launch a doomed attack on Lokhir Fellheart or Lothern, or turning potential Norscan allies against the dark elves. 

## **On Black Tides**
Duriath Helbane needs plunder and captives to prepare for his planned attack on Tor Elithis, and ravaging the Empire’s coastal settlements could provide both. This campaign outline presents the _Temple of Spite_ as an offshore threat. 

## **Part 1 — Predator in the Fog**
The Characters find themselves in the coastal freistadt of Stielstand, as summer turns to autumn and the year’s bounteous harvest is stowed on ships ready for trade. The dockside bustle comes to a halt when a cog drifts into port through the morning mist, its torn sails hanging limply from its mast. No living soul remains on board, and several long, barbed bolts of elegant design pierce the vessel’s hull. 

Over the next week, strange fogs roll in from the sea, more ships go missing, and the burgomeister hires the Characters to investigate. Just east of town, they discover flotsam washed ashore with a lone survivor lashed to a sea chest. He is almost dead and quite insane, raving about ‘the pale ones’ who swept in on their ship, sailing faster than any human vessel. They dragged away his shipmates and left him to die. 

Back in Stielstand, the situation is tense. Sailors refuse to leave port for fear of their lives, while the merchants’ guild puts pressure on their captains to sail before the harvest spoils in their holds. The town is gripped by fear and the burgomeister sends word to the Imperial Navy in Norden. The messenger gets no more than a mile from the town before he is killed. A single warship is in port, the wolfship _Blessed Greta,_ and the Characters can persuade Captain Stark to take them into the fog. As they venture out, they are attacked by a ravenship crewed by Captain Maelrin and her corsairs. Draped from her gunwales are the ensigns of several of the lost ships. 

Despite being outclassed by the wolfship, Maelrin’s corsairs toy with their prey, picking off sailors from the deck with crossbows before sweeping in to rake the _Blessed Greta_ with reaper bolt fire and then retreating into the fog. Maelrin does not risk her ship, preferring to taunt and frighten the humans. As they fend off the ravenship’s assaults, the Characters see something on the horizon, barely visible above the fog, a huge shadow looming high over the waves. The _Temple of Spite_ has come to Ostland. 

The Characters can try to chase the ravenship, to no avail, or they can try again to seek help from the navy, or assist with tensions in town. Defeating Maelrin requires cunning rather than firepower. If they work with locals and offer bait of some kind, they could lure the ravenship onto rocks close to shore, find a way to board, or allow themselves to be taken captive and try to overcome Maelrin’s corsairs. With several vessels they could surround the over-confident Maelrin. If they encounter any corsairs in person, the Druchii laugh and taunt them in accented Reikspiel, claiming they would be better off dying now than continuing to resist. 

## **Part 2 — the Infiltrators**
Stielstand is isolated and vulnerable, as no one dares to leave by sea and messengers are killed. Khaine’s Eyes are responsible, stalking the countryside and coastline, striking isolated farms and settlements to sow terror and demoralise the Ostlanders. 

On the _Temple of Spite_ , the Black Convocation order an invasion of Ostland to seize sacrifices for Khaine and steal captives, Raiding parties land to soften the coastal defences. In this scenario, the Characters investigate the area around Stielstand to discover and thwart Helbane’s preparations for invasion: 

- The Sigmarite monastery of Orlsheim is attacked by corsairs under Captain Qulla. The crew capture the monks, steal several relics, and alchemical ingredients, but leave the gold. 

- Khaine’s Eyes pick off road wardens and patrols of Ostland State troops travelling the Erengrad Road. 

- Valerion’s Blackswords arrive in the small settlement of Wolletz and offer their services as mercenaries to defend the village. When the time is right, they subdue the villagers and move to the next settlement where they make the same offer, telling horrifying stories of what happened in Wolletz. 

- The _Nightwake_ anchors five miles west of Stielstand. Anuidethar Veilthorn heads into town to sell stolen cargos in exchange for silver and reliable charts of the coastline. A greedy merchant, Reinhardt Kess, is desperate to make back his losses from the harvest and may trade with the dark elf, despite his misgivings about whether he is what he claims. 

- A company of dreadspears, the Selekan Guard, assault a party of travellers heading west from the ruins of Haugrvik. One of the survivors claims to be Aesthanil Fleetsong, a sea elf sailor. The Characters could rescue him themselves and hear his offer to come to Stielstand and offer his counsel on the threat from the ark. They may even uncover his real identity, Khardil Ulakth, an agent of the Glass Thorn. 

- East of Stielstand is Wolfila’s Watch, a seafort built high up on the cliffs. The garrison has been stricken by nightmares and waking terrors, summoned by the sorceress Netathi Fellwhisper. 

By uncovering and defeating the infiltrators, the Characters hamper Helbane’s invasion plans. Eventually, they can track Khaine’s Eyes through valleys inland to a row of standing stones, where a small party of dark elves are forcing captives to dig for something. These stones were raised by the elves when they were masters of the Old World and hidden beneath the ground is the Periapt of Lileath, a legendary amulet. Supreme Sorceress Xalthea demands the artefact to power a ritual to make the invasion effortless. The Characters could stop the dark elves from recovering the amulet, set back their invasion plans, and learn more of the ark from freed captives. 

## **Part 3 — the Rite of Dread**
The Supreme Sorceress’s ritual requires several sorceresses to land in Ostland and manipulate the waystones there. She plans a grand invocation of dark power to bring madness and despair to coastal Ostland, rendering the humans helpless in the face of the warhost. When the sorceresses find the stones, each will weave a subtle spell to make the stone sing at dusk, emanating a discordant vibration attuned to the ripples of _Dhar_ . When sufficient waystones are corrupted, their singing unleashes a wave of psychological dread across the region. If the dark elves have the Periapt of Lileath, it amplifies the power of the ritual and its horrifying effects. 

The Characters are sent by the burgomeister to investigate rumours from the nearby hamlet of Lindhof. The peasants are supposedly acting strangely and insist an old stone column has started singing. When the Characters arrive, they find the villagers’ minds ruined by intolerable anguish. Only Mother Hanna, the Rhyan priestess, remains coherent. She can tell the party of a beautiful black-haired elf (Samuril) who enquired about the whereabouts of the waystone. A day later, the stone began to drone. Hiding in the hills is a shepherd who witnessed the elf casting spells at the stone. The Characters can also learn of three similar stones in the area. After Samuril’s success at the first stone, three more sorceresses travel with their guards to these stones, bribing and intimidating locals to find their locations: 

- Rakaria Dran is accompanied by Captain Flariel and three of his Corsairs. 

- Netathi Fellwhisper has a bodyguard of 4 Bleakswords. The Characters may have encountered her earlier at Wolfila’s Watch. 

- Sorceress Mortella travels with Beastmaster Kelrathi, two other Beastmasters and a pack of 6 warhounds. 

- Supreme Sorceress Xalthea waits offshore on Captain Redthorn’s ravenship, ready to complete the ritual when at least three stones are singing. If the dark elves secured the Periapt of Lileath, she keeps it in her cabin. 

As each sorceress scouts the land, they leave evidence of their passing. The Characters can follow their trails and intercept them as they search for the waystones. If they are cunning, they can prevent the ritual or pit the sorceresses against one another. If they prevent Mortella from completing her assignment, she sees an opportunity. The sorceress now believes the invasion is a mistake and intends to turn the situation to her advantage. She describes to the Characters the presence of the _Temple of Spite_ and claims they shall inevitably end up as captives on board when the invasion happens. Having beaten her at the waystone, she sees they would make useful pawns. She offers to act as their protectors on board, if they follow her bidding to discredit the Cult of Khaine. 

If the Characters stop the ritual, the supreme sorceress sails back to the ark in a rage. If they do not, Helbane readies the warhost, beastmasters, and Knives of Khaine for an invasion. 

## **Part 4 — Through the Fog**
If the Characters thwarted the dark elves’ attempts at infiltration and stopped the sorceress’s ritual, the people of Stielstand can finally send word of an immense threat out in the Sea of Claws. The Second Fleet in Nordland can spare a squadron of three wargalleys to accompany the _Blessed Greta,_ and templars of the Order of the Sons of Manaan offer a wargalley from their chapter house in Salkalten, complete with a complement of knights. 

The Characters set out on a naval expedition to find the source of Ostland’s woes. The _Temple of Spite_ far outclasses their little fleet, though if they use good judgement, they can damage the dark elf fleet and further deter Helbane from his plans for invasion. 

The flotilla is an uneasy alliance of ships and crews with their own motives, rivalries, and fears. As they navigate through the fog, the Characters must overcome rifts amongst the captains and crews to forge an effective fighting force. 

- The captain of the _Blessed Greta_ is Wilbert Stark, supposedly in command of the flotilla. Stark is frankly terrified after his encounter with Captain Maelrin’s ravenship, which makes him indecisive and eager for direction from the Characters. First mate Lutz Wolfhart is ensorcelled by Netathi Fellwhisper to betray the ship at a crucial moment. 

- Templar Captain Gunter Ahlers commands the _Kraken’s Wrath_ and his templar marines. The Sons of Manann are brave, headstrong, and reluctant to follow orders from Captain Stark. 

- The wargalleys are _Sigmar’s Wrath, Reliant,_ and _The Brazen Sabre_ . Captain Grünstret of _Sigmar’s Wrath_ does not believe the Ostlanders face any real threat, while Captain von Bache of the _Reliant_ is a young woman keen to prove herself. 

The fleet must navigate the fog and face strange encounters in search of the ark: 

- On a tiny unnamed island far from the coast, Captain Flariel’s corsairs are taking on fresh water when the Character’s vessels happen upon them. 

- A Bjornling longship limps through the fog after surviving an attack by dark elves. The crew burn for revenge and will join the Characters’ ships if asked. A ship full of furious Norscans could prove very useful. 

- If Captain Maelrin survived the first scenario, her ravenship still lurks on the sea. When she recognises the _Blessed Greta_ , she tries to pick off some wargalleys before returning to the ark to summon the fleet 

- Anselm is a hermit who dwells on a windswept rock many miles from the coast. He saw _Temple of Spite_ nearby the day before and will happily tell the Characters about it. Unfortunately, Anselm is a follower of Stromfels who prays that the Characters, their fleet, and the dark elves all die horribly at sea. 

- Another missing ship appears on the horizon as the sun sets. _Rhya’s Bounty_ lost all hands to the dark elves and now the souls of the dead haunt the ship. The ghosts are mournful and resent the living, though they could recount their ordeal if the Characters are able to listen. 

- Captain Manbane commands a pack of three doomreavers in the waters close to _Temple of Spite_ . The ferocious helldrakes are hungry for battle, so their beastmaster handlers and Manbane struggle to restrain them from attacking anything they encounter. 

The Characters, and any survivors, eventually come in sight of the _Temple of Spite_ . Its sheer size makes an attack ill-advised, though they may have an opportunity to get aboard. The Norscans or Sons of Manann may attack impetuously and create a distraction, allowing the Characters to climb into the ark (see page 30). Instead, they could be captured by one of the corsair vessels and dragged aboard as captives. Mortella could scry their location and find a way to get them aboard, as she looks forward to toying with her new pawns. 

## **Part 5 — the Sorceress’s Playthings**
The Characters now have a choice of several courses of action. They could creep aboard the _Temple of Spite_ and find a means to deter the invasion. They may flee from the ark to return to the mainland, raise the alarm and seek a larger fleet, or try to warn the Empire’s military of the imminent invasion. 

Once on board the black ark, they can accept Mortella’s patronage. She adopts them as her personal servants and magically inscribes her sigil onto their faces to warn other dark elves of her protection. In exchange, they must advance her schemes to harm the Khainites on board and sway the Black Convocation to act against the invasion. Mortella expects the Characters to show initiative rather than merely enact her orders, so she does not provide many specific instructions. 

Humiliating the Khainites is challenging, though their unpopularity on board _Temple of Spite_ helps. The witch elves take various potions and draughts to induce frenzy and bring them closer to Khaine, so Mortella proposes switching these for hallucinogenic substances, and the tensions outlined on page 113 provide opportunities to drive a wedge between prominent Khainites. The Characters could further discredit them by goading Hulreth into murdering one of the black ark’s prominent dark elves. 

Members of the Black Convocation are eminently corruptible, and Mortella knows many secrets. She’s willing to share these with the Characters if it suits her purposes. Gradually, the Characters can turn the dark elves’ desires away from the Old World, to the extent that even Duriath Helbane grows weary of the idea. If successful, Mortella intends to celebrate by offering the Characters as delectable sacrifices to Nzandra the Tormentor at the next rite of Slaanesh. 

The Characters could work to sink _Temple of Spite_ , a difficult but not impossible endeavour. It’s also conceivable that this final scenario leads in to **The Seaborne Citadel** and takes the Characters towards Ulthuan, starting with **Part 3 — Amongst the Druchii** (page 35). 

However they deal with the threat of _Temple of Spite_ , the Characters need to escape somehow. There are ships in the dock which they could steal or some of their fleet may have been captured intact. Of course, they _could_ fail to prevent the invasion. In this case, Ostland, and the Characters have plenty to worry about. A military campaign follows, in which the party’s nowextensive knowledge of the invaders could prove an invaluable asset to the state troops deployed to protect the province. 

## **The Helbane Standard**
Duriath helbane’s personal banner is dominated by a symbolic representation of a fleshless corsair’s head, adorned with a helm incorporating the batlike wings of a manticore, a monstrous creature considered by many dark elves to be an aspect of Khaine and so worthy of veneration. 

This device is common to the helbane family, though on Duriath’s banner, the helm is inscribed with the rune of Mathlann, the elven god of the seas. Whilst Mathlann is not one of the gods of the underworld commonly worshipped by the dark elves, many corsairs consider it wise to pay him respect as they venture within his domain. 

The Druchast runes for slaughter and murder are also displayed on Duriath’s banner, and provide a fair statement of intent given the habits of the corsairs under his command. They are also a boast that the fleetmaster enjoys the good graces of both Lord Venil Chillblade (whose own banner prominently displays the rune for slaughter) and Lady Drane Brackblood (whose best silver diadem is inscribed with the rune for murder). 

## **Bestiary**
## **Dark Elves**
The Druchii are tall, slender, and graceful like all elves and share the angular features and cold beauty of their high elf kin. Likewise, they have the same natural agility and heightened reactions, moving with feline agility and precision, each action an exercise in elegant purpose. Dark elves’ adult physiques are honed through a lifetime of training, resulting in lean, wiry muscle rather than brute strength. 

Elven eyes are large and oval, staring with a disturbing, otherworldly wisdom. Dark elves commonly have icy blue, violet, and jet black eye colours. All elves have pale skin, but Druchii flesh is unusually colourless, thanks to the thin sunlight _Dhar_ permeating of Naggaroth and the damaging effects of their environs. This cadaverous pallor disappears in healthier climes, so a dark elf could conceivably pass for Asur, Asrai, or Eonir if they choose. Druchii hair tends toward darker tones, a legacy of their Nagarythe heritage. Blonde and auburn hair is rare, but not unknown. 

The concept of yenlui concerns harmony between the light and dark aspects of the elven spirit. By favouring Khaine and the Cytharai, dark elves disdain the need for balance and give themselves over to malevolence. This corrupts and corrodes their spirit, so Druchii find ways to divert harm from themselves — they invoke small, almost unconscious, pacts with their gods and other dark entities to counter the loss of physical resilience and will. 

Despite a culture of dominance and subjugation that rejects softer feelings, dark elves are not entirely sociopathic. They can experience regret, feel anxiety, uncertainty, and sympathy. Camaraderie and friendship persist even in Naggarothi society, and while romantic attachment lacks overt affection, it is no less real. Dark elves can even trust, though this is fragile.  There is tragedy inherent to Druchii 

life, for they want more than 

cruelty, but to display kindness 

or compassion implies weakness, which is a death sentence in their society. 

Elves are all long-lived and age has little effect on their appearance, though the dangers of life in Druchii society often leaves scars. These are worn with pride, proof that they have faced adversaries and bested them. 

## **Psychology**
Dark elf culture encourages a nihilistic and deeply individualistic worldview, shaped by ancient hatreds, cultural paranoia, and ruthless ambition. Their psychology is defined by a need for dominance and the weaponisation of intense emotions. As elves, the Druchii experience of joy, rage, sorrow, and ecstasy alike are heightened to dangerous extremes. They take pleasure in cruelty, finding beauty in suffering, and seek fulfilment through relentless personal indulgence. Prone to obsession, a dark elf may devote decades, or even centuries, to a single consuming passion, whether it be vengeance, excess, the study of a field of knowledge, or the mastery of a chosen art. 

Dark elves value intelligence and cunning for both survival and domination; eloquence and deceit are cultivated as art forms and tools. This includes humour, and there is a cynical, wry wit common to dark elves, conveyed in their conversation and acts of amusing viciousness. 

Paranoia pervades every facet of life, for it is said that Malerion sees all and this belief keeps the Druchii in a state of ceaseless vigilance, ever fearful that a careless word or deed might betray disloyalty. Should the Dread King’s sorcery and hidden eyes fail to uncover your actions, it is all but certain that a rival will do _hithuan,_ or etiquette. so in his stead. Paranoia also influences Lowborn may not approach within three sword lengths of a noble unless summoned. The more trusted the retainer, the closer they may approach, though only lovers and playthings can come within arm’s reach. 

Druchii attitudes towards Chaos are complex, as they believe they can harness its power without being consumed. To them, Chaos is both raw potential and the ultimate peril, a force that threatens to erase individuality and autonomy if left unchecked. It is not something to be worshipped, but exploited, mastered, and in time overcome, for, in their boundless arrogance, the dark elves truly believe they can outwit daemons. 

## **A Question of Upbringing**
Sixty-five years ago, Lady Liraeth Winterthorn thought it amusing to test whether Asur are inherently different to Druchii and so ordered a high elf baby stolen during a raid on Rokhame. Raised as her own son, Thanis Winterthorn is now as cruel as his peers and distinguishable only by his white blonde hair. When Elarion Seaflame reached adulthood in Rokhame, he swore to track down the dark elves who took his twin. After many years of searching, Elarion traced the raiders to _Temple of Spite_ . His Cothiqui acquaintances tell him this is a foolhardy obsession, but an elven captain in Marienburg just told him where the ark might be found. Now he needs to find a party of adventurers equally foolhardy to chase down the _Temple of Spite_ and help him get aboard. 

## **Presentation**
Dark elves choose clothing and personal ornament with care, each piece carrying meaning, whether as an implied invocation to the Cytharai, or as subtle protection from damaging effects of dark yenlui. Barbed decorations and curved jewellery are crafted to mimic the sinuous tendrils of flowing _Dhar_ . Body piercings and _keikalla_ (spirit bells) align in careful arrangement to invoke the gods and repel malevolent spirits. Most dark elves wear their hair long, often braided with metal threads. 

Vanity is a common vice, from the lowest to the highest strata of society, and nowhere is this more clearly expressed than in dress. Clothing speaks volumes about a dark elf ’s relative status, and even most functional attire is meticulously cut, regardless of fabric or style. In cities, rigid sumptuary laws dictate who may wear what, shaped as much by a ruler’s personal aesthetic whims as by a deliberate reinforcement of social division. Almost every Druchii owns a cloak to keep out Naggaroth’s chill, often worn over a padded coat, while the wealthy and knightly classes wear _khaitans,_ garments fashioned from exotic silks or the flensed hides of humans or dwarfs. Many dark 

elves wear light chain shirts under their cloaks, because violence is an accepted constant of life. Elaborate metal diadems and headdresses mark high status, yet such adornments are forbidden to commoners, save within the blood-soaked strictures of the Cult of Khaine. 

## **Language**
Dark elves speak a dialect of Elthárin known as Druhir or ‘Black Elven’. This variant originated from Nagarythe, and over the years it acquired many loan words from Dark Tongue, the language of Chaos spoken by tribes of the northern wastes. It is a lyrical, expressive language with countless subtleties and nuances. Many of the tonal aspects of Elthárin have twisted over millennia, producing a flatter, more discordant sound. 

The Druchii understand other dialects of Elthárin, though they may choose to speak in a Druhir dialect so thick that other elves struggle comprehend it. Autarii tribes have their own feral variant of Druhir that sounds harsh and unsophisticated in Naggaroth’s cities.

## **Cold Ones**
Called _‘nauglir’_ in the Druhir dialect, cold ones live in the caves beneath Hag Graef. Their chill flesh is almost immune to pain, and their bodies exude a foul-smelling slime. Though singleminded when hunting, cold ones are stubborn and slow witted, so it takes great strength and willpower to master such a steed. They will not allow a rider unless they mask their own smell with _vrasha_ (see page 59).

## **Anath Raema, the Savage Huntress**
Anath Raema is the sister of Khaine and the goddess of the savage hunt. Through her, the dark elves are gifted the joy of the chase and of the kill. Anath Raema does not care who or what is hunted, as every living creature is prey to the bloodthirsty goddess. 

The Savage Huntress is a vengeful deity, who wears a belt of heads and hands about her waist. These are tokens claimed from hunters who bore her blessings but offered no praise in return. Legend also tells that her amorous advances were once spurned by Kurnous, and so she is worshipped by some elves as a patron of jealous lovers, an avenging deity who will hunt down and slay those who have wronged her supplicants.

## **Creature Trait: Many Heads (Number)**
**The creature has more than one head. If a Critical Wound affecting the head stuns, kills, or renders the creature unconscious it will only affect the creature once all the heads are either disabled or affected to a similar degree. If the creature has the Bite, Horns, or Tongue Traits it can make a number of free attacks equal to the number of healthy heads. The creature benefits from +2 SL to Perception Tests whilst it has at least two healthy heads.**

The winged beasts known as harpies are not native to Naggaroth. They originated in the Mountains of Mourn and, at some point in the past, an outcast flock found its way to the mountains around Karond Kar and built their nests in the peaks. Batwinged and limber, these savage creatures follow raiding fleets for months in hope of a good meal, and it is no surprise that many choose to make their nests in the lofty towers of black arks. 

Some claim harpies are the souls of slain witch elves given physical form, while others state they are a manifestation of the Bloody-handed God himself. They are certainly vicious enough for either explanation to be true, as harpies have a similar temperament to dark elves and delight in tormenting their victims. Particularly enterprising or foolhardy dark elves have been known to leave lures for harpies, setting the creatures upon their enemies, and the sight of a flock of harpies tearing a hapless sea elf or captive apart is a favoured entertainment for many of a black ark’s inhabitants. 

**Belligerent:** As long as they possess Advantage and their opponent does not, they are immune to _Fear_ . 

**Bestial:** Animal behaviour is simple and predictable, see the **WFRP Core Rulebook** . 

**Fly 60:** As the creature’s Move, they can fly up to 60 yards, see the **WFRP Core Rulebook** for details. 

**Hungry:** If they incapacitate an opponent or encounter a fresh body, they must pass an **Average (+20) Cool** Test or feast, losing their next Move and Action. 

**Infected:** Wounded opponents must take an **Easy (+40) Endurance** Test to avoid a _Festering Wound_ . 

In Naggarothi lore, harpies are an omen of good fortune. It is said that if they ever desert Karond Kar, the city would fall soon after. This belief has carried over to black arks and there are many dark elf sailors who would not set foot upon one if they saw no harpies aboard. Harsh punishments await any who raise their hand against a ship’s harpies, and many would rather let the monsters carry them away than face retribution. 

**Night Vision:** See clearly for 20 yards and extend the illumination distance of light sources by 20 yards. 

**Skittish:** Receive +3 _Broken_ Conditions  if affected by loud noise or magic. 

_Temple of Spite_ boasts a fine flock of harpies, their blackfeathered forms flitting constantly between the towers, on the lookout for unwary prey. Their care is of considerable importance to all aboard: the followers of Khaine hold them in reverence; the sorceresses use pieces of their dead in rituals; and corsairs trust the harpies to lead them to fresh prey. To be tasked with their care is considered a sign of great favour among the beastmasters. In truth, it is one of the most unpleasant and dangerous jobs aboard. 

## **Fiends That Plague Thee**
Harpy corpses have appeared on deck, their skin bleached and leprous. A disease is spreading and many worry what might happen should all the harpies die, so Beastmaster Kelrathi plans to send a group of captives into the eyries to find the source and clear out the infected. The Characters are ‘volunteered’ to lead the way. 

## **Helldrakes**
Helldrakes are sinuous sea serpents with dragon-like heads and a maw lined with spine-like teeth. Pack hunters who overcome their marine prey through animal cunning and tenacious ferocity, helldrakes are known to devolve into feeding frenzies, churning the water into bloody froth as they fight for choice morsels. They reside in Naggaroth’s shallower waters, following raiding ships to feed off the bounty of dead they leave behind. 

In Clar Karond, some beastmasters dedicate their lives to these beasts, raising them with their packmates until they can serve as attack beasts, and so helldrake eggs are a valued prize. Juveniles are used in marine hunting packs or to pull small vessels, while the largest and strongest are harnessed to small dark elf ships as ‘doomreavers’. To command a doomreaver is a high honour for a beastmaster — they stand proudly on their beast’s neck, directing them with savage jabs of agonising lances. Even so, a helldrake is a near impossible creature to predict, as liable to attack its allies as its enemy, and great shame awaits any handler who allows their foul-tempered mount to slip control.

## **From Hell’s Heart**
Sorceress Mortella requires a helldrake’s heart, but the creatures are too valuable to the beastmasters and corsairs for her to kill one herself. She needs one to sicken and intends to place her own captive agents aboard a doomreaver to administer poison. 

## **Sea Dragons**
Sea dragons are among the ocean’s largest creatures. They hold a striking resemblance to their airborne kin, but their bodies are bloated and wingless, adapted to chill waters. Their oncemighty limbs are now claw-tipped flippers, while their long, serpentine tails churn the water into frothing foam. They are capable of tearing apart ships with their teeth or smashing them to splinters with their tail. Whether they were true dragons corrupted by dark magic or a separate species is unknown; their minds are bestial and closed to all. 

There are stories of sailors making camp on craggy islands, only to be dragged under when the sea dragon dives; indeed some beastmasters build fortresses upon their backs, which is a dangerous practice given the creatures’ short tempers. Dark elves do have an affinity for the beasts and to hunt or command one is a mark of great status. Sea dragons only come onto land once or twice in their long lifetimes to lay eggs, choosing remote coastal caves as lairs. When such a nest is discovered, dark elves flock to the site, fighting each other to claim the eggs. When a sea dragon dies, its corpse is in great demand for spell ingredients and the tough hide, used by corsairs for their cloaks. 

**SEA DRAGON**

## **Druchii Anointed**
In the years before the Sundering, Morathi encouraged Cults of Pleasure in Ulthuan dedicated to the worship of Slaanesh. When the dark elves settled in Naggaroth, Malerion outlawed these cults in favour of the Cult of Khaine, reasoning that the elven god of murder and war could forge his people into a sword directed at the hated high elves of Ulthuan, while desire and pleasure were selfish and weakened his people’s will. 

Despite the witch elves’ efforts to eradicate worship of the Dark Prince, Slaanesh’s influence persists among the Druchii to this day thanks largely to the protection afforded the Dark Prince’s cult by the sorceress Morathi. As she worked to safeguard her son’s place as ruler of the dark elves, Morathi made unwholesome pacts with Slaanesh to perfect her control of Dark Magic. 

The Anointed were once known as the _dru perim_ , or ‘Dark Pilgrims’, participants in Slaaneshi rites where they were anointed with the Dark Prince’s essence. They followed Morathi and her son to Naggaroth after the Sundering, but when the Cult of Pleasure was forbidden, the Anointed fought their oppressors and refused to forsake their god. They set out to cross into the Chaos Wastes, where they battled the servants of the other Chaos Gods, eager for each new sensation. 

Through centuries of battle, their numbers were severely reduced until only a handful remained. These ancient champions battle still, occasionally venturing south past the watch towers to corrupt their kin and taunt the Cult of Khaine. Some remain in Naggaroth to inspire secret cults, or travel abroad to corrupt elves wherever they settle. Nzandra the Tormentor is one such Anointed, living on _Temple of Spite_ (see page 29). 

Most elves are resistant to physical mutation, but some among the Anointed show signs of long exposure to the energies of Chaos. Their eyes may be completely black, their skin turned pale blue, translucent, or ebony. They are supernatural creatures, capable of terrifying feats of daemonic strength, speed, and agility. 

**Night Vision:** See clearly for 20 yards and extend the illumination distance of light sources by 20 yards. 

**Size (Monstrous):** See the **WFRP Core Rulebook** for implications of size.

**Mark of Slaanesh:** Slaanesh has marked this creature with a physical brand, proclaiming them precious to him. The creature gains the _Fearless (Everything)_ Talent. This creature gains the _Etiquette (Followers of Slaanesh)_ Talent and is subject to _Animosity_ towards overt followers of Khorne. The creature is also subject to _Animosity_ by followers of Khorne, so long as the Mark of Slaanesh is visible. Additionally, they may purchase the following Talents as if they were Career Advances for the normal XP costs: _Attractive_ , _Blather_ , _Careful Strike_ , _Combat Master_ , _Gregarious_ , _Inspiring_ , _Lightning Reflexes_ , _Nimblefingered_ , _Resistant (Poison)_ , and _Sharp_ .

## **Doomfire Warlocks**
Doomfire warlocks know their souls will be claimed by Slaanesh and seek constantly to delay their fates. They yearn for distraction, desperate to forget the horrific reality of their existence, if only for a moment. 

All elves fear having their souls consumed by Slaanesh at death, but for doomfire warlocks it is a pressing matter, as they suffer from Malerion’s curse of hollowness. Due to the Prophecy of Demise, the Dread King fears male sorcerers, and as the grip of his curse tightens, traces of unholy fire creep across a warlock’s skin, blazing into life as dark runes. Once a warlock’s body is swathed in flame, his soul is stolen by the Dark Prince, but the process can be stalled if he sacrifices others in his stead. For such purposes, the purer the soul, the better. 

Doomfire warlocks fall upon villages in the dead of night, seeking victims. Cloaked in shadow, they pass like phantoms through defences, stealing prey from their beds before vanishing. When a dark elf army musters, the warlocks gather. Hoping for captives, they infuse their blades with numbing curses that strip a foe of their sense with a single scratch. Alive but mindless, the victims are led from the battlefield to be sacrificed to Slaanesh.

## **The Thankless Child**
Supreme Sorceress Kalethra believes in keeping her family close, specifically her father Liraen. She discovered his skill with magic when she was a child and cheerfully betrayed him to Malerion. Now he resides, chained, in her chambers, cursed to live as a doomfire warlock and endure his daughter’s mockery. From time to time, she offers him a captive or enemy’s soul to keep his soul from Slaanesh. Liraen dearly wants to escape his torment and may even forgo a sacrifice if they could help him loose his bonds.

## **Witch Elf**
## **Hekarti, Mistress of Magic**
Hekarti is the goddess of Conjurations and dark magic. She sees all the Winds of Magic and has six arms to carry her sacred accoutrements — a serpent-headed staff, a beating heart, a scorpion, a broken arrow, a serrated dagger, and a phial of orphan’s tears. 

Unlike many of her kind, Hekarti pays close attention to the desires of the elves. She is forever locked in jealous contest with her twin sister Atherti, the Goddess of Pleasure, and resents her sway over mortals. It was supposedly this rivalry that first enticed Hekarti to grant wisdom to Morathi. That said, the Hag Sorceress has been careful to keep her devotions to the two sisters in balance, as legends tell of the grim fate of those who favoured one above the other. 

Known also as the ‘Brides of Khaine’ and the _maibd_ , witch elves are Khaine’s acolytes, living only to experience the ecstatic frenzy of murder and to offer hearts — ripped beating from sacrifices — to their god.
